# tests/fixtures — shared test fixtures (WP-fix)

Every file here is synthetic. No row, summary or payload comes from a real session. Owner: WP-fix (`OWNERS.tsv`), except `assembly/expected/`, which `tools/assemble --goldens` writes.

`tools/fixtures-gen` renders the fixtures into `plugin/tests/unit/_gen/{brand,corpus,payloads}.gen.ts` for U tests (the kit has no fs). `tools/fixtures-gen --check` runs the WP-fix exit checks: every JSON file and JSONL line parses, `expected.tsv` matches the reference detector, no secret-shaped string sits in any file, the generated files are current, every `setups/` recipe builds and builds what it claims, no short time sits in any fixture text (RV-24, below), and a renamed temp copy passes after the plain regenerate step.

## Placeholders

| Token | Filled by | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `{{plugin}}`, `{{marketplace}}` | `tools/fixtures-gen` (U), the case runner (H) | `brand.json` `name`, `marketplace` |
| `$TMP`, `$HOME`, `$ROOT`, `$WATCH`, `$SID` | case runner | the case's temp dir, fresh HOME, handoff root, watch dir, `ids.json` `sid.S1` |
| `$FIXTURES` | case runner | absolute path of `tests/fixtures` |
| `$BRAND`, `$LSTART1` | case runner | `brand.json` `name`; the start time `ps` prints for pid 1 (a process that is alive on every machine, so a record naming it is a live owner) |
| `$SECRET{<id>}` | case runner only | the joined fragments of `secrets/corpus.json` entry `<id>` |
| `$NONCE` (any `$<VAR>` a step captured) | case runner | the value an earlier step's `capture` took from its stdout (`sequences/S-21-classic`) |

A file holding `$SECRET{` is never copied into a generated module.

## Formats

**Payloads.** Keys are exactly the d.ts classic input types (`PreCompactHookInput` … `PermissionDeniedHookInput`, 2.1.305). `prompt_id` is left out where TF Q2 §1 says it is absent (SessionStart startup, resume, clear, fork). `permission_mode` is left out of PreCompact, PostCompact and SessionStart (lab key sets). `transcript_path` is `$TMP/projects/-tmp-example-repo/<sid>.jsonl`, and `cwd` is `$TMP/example-repo`. One exception is deliberate: `PostCompact/extra-key.json` adds `fixture_extra_key` (AT-M3-11).

**Corpus.** Each `.txt` file is the raw text as PostCompact (`<summary>…</summary>`) or the mod (`This session is being continued…` wrapper) sees it. `expected.tsv` columns: `file`, `verdict`, `marker_line`, `sentinel_from_end`, `nonce`, `scope`, `normalized_sha256`, `dispatch`, `sentinel_place` (`inside`, `after-close`, P5-FOLD A1). `-` means not found. `dispatch` is empty for text alone, `none` for a PostCompact with no dispatch at all, or a `watch/` record path for this compaction. The reference detector in `tools/fixtures-gen` fixes the readings below. The TS and helper detectors must give the same tuple (AT-C-03).
- Head stripping repeats over the leading lines: blank lines, the `This session is being continued` line, the `<tools-used-before-summary>` block, a `Summary:` line and a `<summary>` tag. So the marker after the full wrapper is body line 1 (AT-C-02 a).
- The body ends before the first `</summary>`. Sentinel after the close tag (MOD-SPEC §5.1, P5-FOLD A1): when the first non-blank text after `</summary>` (the rest of that line, else the next non-blank line) is our sentinel, that line becomes the body's last line, and the lines after it follow it as trailers; any other first line keeps everything after the tag outside the body (38). Listed trailers (spec and canary-baseline `copy_trailers`, both empty today, plus a table's own `copy_trailers.json`) are cut from the end, never the moved sentinel; with no `</summary>` the same cut applies to the body's end. `sentinel_place` is `after-close` when the sentinel found is that moved line. Trailing blank lines are trimmed. Line ends become `\n`. The normalized body is the lines joined by `\n` plus one final `\n` (empty body: empty string). `normalized_sha256` is computed over that text with `{{plugin}}` filled.
- The marker is the first anchored match in body lines 1–5. The sentinel is searched in the last 3 non-blank lines, and `sentinel_from_end` is reported whenever one is found there, also for `unshaped`.
- With a dispatch, the checks run in this order: `stale` (marker nonce ≠ the dispatch nonce; or dispatch `none` and a marker), then `scope-leak` (dispatch `agent_id` set and `s=main` or a `## Resume here` heading, with any marker or none (41); dispatch main, meaning `agent_id` null with channel `mod-hook` or `mod-self` (MOD §2.4 P1), and `s=sub`; a `classic` dispatch proves neither scope), then the text verdicts.
- The corpus brand is `{{plugin}}`, so the sha column changes with a rename. The plain regenerate step `tools/fixtures-gen` (BUILD-PLAN §4.6) rewrites that column for the current brand, so a rename commits `expected.tsv` with the other regenerated files. `--check` runs the same rename in a temp copy (check `rename`).

Sub-tables: `summaries/p5/` and `summaries/acuity/` each hold their own `expected.tsv` in the same columns, so the 41-file corpus of AT-C-03 (the TS test pins the count) does not change. A reader of `p5/expected.tsv` adds `p5/copy_trailers.json` to the shipped trailer lists (09 is cut to 17's body). The P5 texts are the lab run's PostCompact `compact_summary` with the run folder written as `/tmp/example-repo`, the brand as `{{plugin}}`, log times in the ISO `T` form (RV-24) and `key=` in quoted log lines as `k=` (secret scan); the sentinel placement is untouched. In `p5/`, 09 and 12 share 17's normalized body. `tools/fixtures-gen` renders them as `CORPUS_P5`, `P5_COPY_TRAILERS` and `CORPUS_ACUITY` in `corpus.gen.ts`.

Groups worth knowing: 01–05, 11, 27, 29 and 38 share one normalized body (PostCompact, mod wrapper with and without tags, bare, CRLF, blank tail, leading blanks, text after `</summary>`), and so do 17 and 18 (subagent). 37 adds an unlisted trailer to the mod form only. Its PostCompact twin is 01 (AT-M3-17).

**Dispatch roles** (`watch/dispatch-<nonce>.json`, all S1 unless noted): `1a2b3c4d` mod-hook main auto midturn · `2b3c4d5e` mod-self plugin · `3c4d5e6f` and `bc1d2e3f` (2 s later) classic · `4d5e6f70` precompute · `5e6f7081`, `6f708192`, `708192a3` subagents A1–A3 · `8192a3b4` mod-hook main manual, pending, for the unmarked defer (AT-M3-15) · `5ca1ab1e` an earlier main dispatch · `9a0b1c2d` auto, and `ab0c1d2e` precompute, both 11 min old (AT-M3-06) · `d2e3f405` main in the second process P2 (AT-M5-04) · `d3e4f506` session S3 (AT-M5-03). `0badf00d` has no record on purpose (AT-C-10). `da24cc4a`, `f5d2ccf6`, `d2158267`, `4dae03c4`, `228e0cc9`, `084ad868`: the six classic dispatches of P5-replay. `1d1e0c0a`: the idle mod-hook main auto dispatch (`idle: true`; `dispatch-1d1e0c0a-not-idle.json` is the same record with `idle: false`, seeded under the nonce name).

**Transcripts.** Summary rows written by the engine (lab P5 on 2.1.307, the owner's 2.1.306 sessions) carry no `<summary>` tags and end with three engine trailer lines after the body (`If you need specific details from before compaction …`, `Continue the conversation from where it left off …`, `The messages after this summary are the most recent messages …`). The P5-replay, fill-joins and idle summary rows use that form; the older synthetic rows (S-21, T-NN) do not. No `copy_trailers` list names these lines (core cuts them only in its transcript-row reader, `transcript.pm`, option b of fix-escalations item 1), so a reader that normalizes a summary row without cutting them gets the trailers in the body: the sentinel sits 4th from the end and the body sha differs from the PostCompact copy. `tools/fixtures-gen --check` runs `manifests`: each manifest's payloads equal their corpus files, every PostCompact body line is a line of its summary row, the records, sizes and hook times agree, and `idle-cases.json` expectations follow the IC-1 D1 rule (idle = mod or native; source `both`/`mod`/native/`none`; one mismatch when they disagree). The runner copies `main.jsonl` to the payload's `transcript_path`, and `subagents/` to `<session dir>/subagents/`, where the session dir is the transcript path without `.jsonl`. `main.part-NN.jsonl` files are appended in step order, so turn ends (Stop events) fall between rows (T-12, T-25). Timestamps are UTC (`Z`). The case clock is +03:00. One line in `T-16/main.jsonl` is malformed on purpose.

**Watcher cases.** `input.json` holds: `seed` (files to copy before the first step; `to` starts with `$WATCH` or `$ROOT`), `repo` (a recipe), `transcripts`, optional `transcript_mode` and `unreadable` (paths to create with mode 000), and `steps`. Each step has `now`, `argv`, `stdin`, an optional `transcript_append`, and `expect` (`exit`, plus `stdout`; `null` means not asserted). `expected.json` quotes the WATCH §9 row, names the v1 scope (BUILD-PLAN §5.2), and lists `asserts` in the §3.5 case vocabulary: `rows` (file, `ev`, `fields`, `count`), `absent_rows`, `files`, `grep_absent`. `metrics` gives the spec's metric values for fields that WATCH §6.3 does not name on a row. WP-watch maps those.

**Sequences.** `sequences/<id>/input.json` uses the watcher `input.json` keys plus three. `transcript_state` (`{boundaries, summaries}`) is the main transcript's `compact_boundary` and `isCompactSummary` row count when that step's hook fires, after its `transcript_append`, which is appended before the step runs. `capture` is the runner's `{VAR: "re:<regex>"}` from the step's stdout, used as `$VAR` in later payloads and transcript parts. `"order": "S-21"` makes `--check` require that SessionStart(compact) and PostCompact see no boundary row newer than PreCompact. `transcript_bytes_min` on a step makes `--check` require at least that many transcript bytes when the step runs (the 512 KB budget case), and a step `expect` may carry `ms_max` (the case vocabulary). `expected.json` gives `observed_order`, and `step_asserts` (`after_step` plus `files`, `rows`, `absent_rows` in the §3.5 vocabulary, each with a `why`). Three keys are new for AT-WD-11: a `files` entry with `snapshot: <label>` records the matched file's bytes after that step, and `same_bytes_as: <label>` asserts the file still has exactly those bytes; `joined` lists the rollup row as `rollup::rows` returns it after the nonce join (sizes plus `join_conflict`, 0 or 1 per nonce); a top-level `metrics` gives a `status` count the case maps. The case runner (`tests/helper/run.pl`, WP-core) replays a sequence for a case `{"sequence": "<id>"}`: `step_asserts` join the expect of the step they follow, `absent_rows` become `rows_absent`, an assert's `fields_ge` goes on its last `rows` entry that names fields, and `metrics.join_conflict` adds a `status` step. `transcript_state` and `transcript_bytes_min` are read by `--check` only. `run.pl --fixtures DIR` reads these fixtures from another checkout's `tests/fixtures` (core-to-fix 1, 2).
- **References.** `--check` recomputes every pinned value from the replayed transcript and the step times, so a wrong pin fails: BD-3 (`proof` P1 for a seeded mod-hook/mod-self main dispatch, else P3 when a main boundary row after the compaction's PreCompact count lands within `MAIN_WINDOW_S` of its PostCompact, else `none`; `proof_lag_ms` = that row's time minus the PostCompact step time, in the lab 12-42 ms range under the S-21 order; an unproven stash must be at least `SETTLE_S` old at the deciding Stop, and `fields_ge.settle_waited_ms` must lie between 0 and its age); E.1 `turn_kind` (a pending record from a deferred PostCompact qualifies when its time is after the last Stop step, no earlier Stop has saved its copy, meaning proved it or found it `SETTLE_S` old, and a main boundary row starting inside the last 512 KiB lies in [ts − 2 s, ts + 600 s]); E.2 `compaction_boundary` sizes, `precomputed` and `cc_version` from the matched row, one per nonce; the rollup sizes as their writer fills them (mod path: PostCompact's own-boundary read, the newest main row no older than the dispatch time minus 1 s; classic: reconcile, from the matched row) and the `joined` view (a null field takes the boundary value, a non-null one is kept, `join_conflict` 1 when a kept value disagrees).
- The S-21 order (lab `E1/probes/S-21-S-26.md` §3, 2.1.306, one manual and one auto run): mod before-step, PreCompact, the summarizer fork's SubagentStop (`agent_type` empty), SessionStart(compact), PostCompact, mod after-step. Only then do the boundary row and the summary row reach the main transcript, so both hooks see 0 of each. The next Stop is the first hook that sees them. `transcripts/S-21-*/main.part-02.jsonl` is what lands after PostCompact. The summary row's own timestamp is earlier than SessionStart, so row timestamps cannot order writes against hooks.
- `S-21-classic` (the AT-C-11 fixture): no mod, so PreCompact writes a classic dispatch and the summary carries its nonce (`$NONCE`, captured from PreCompact stdout). Inside PostCompact there is no proof (F2-1), so the asserts are: no main-slot copy and no sweep, the stash is kept, and after Stop the summary is in the main slot (P3 at reconcile).
- `S-21-mod`: the mod's dispatch `1a2b3c4d` is seeded, P1 proves main inside PostCompact, and after Stop there is still exactly one copy. Step 6 (a second Stop) adds no second `compaction_boundary` row, and the copy keeps mode 0400, its bytes and its frontmatter without `tokens_before`/`tokens_after` (AT-WD-11).
- `S-21-mod-conflict` (AT-WD-11, synthetic): part-01 ends with a main boundary row stamped 0.5 s before the mod dispatch (preTokens 198000, no summary row), so PostCompact's own-boundary read fills the rollup sizes from it; the Stop's reconcile matches the real row (223438) and writes `compaction_boundary` from it. Only `pre_tokens` differs, so `join_conflict` is 1 whether a reader counts nonces or fields. The kept value is 198000.
- `S-21-pd` (AT-WD-10): the positive at step 5, and a confounded negative at step 7 (that Stop both moved last-stop and saved the copy). `S-21-pd-stale` isolates "record older than the last Stop": a Stop 20 ms after the deferred PostCompact, before the boundary row lands, saves nothing (no proof, stash younger than `SETTLE_S`), then the PermissionDenied reads `other`. `S-21-pd-512k` is the positive with 329 earlier session rows in front (551 KB at step 5, the boundary row in the last 4 KB), `ms_max` 2000. `S-21-pd-noboundary` and `S-21-pd-sub` are the other two negatives.

**Repo recipes.** `{v, id, dir, git, branch, author, commits: [{message, files}], dirty, untracked, ignored_files, note}`; `git: false` recipes have `files` only. A `.gitignore` in the first commit holds the ignored patterns. Commits use the fixed author and date in the recipe.

**Temp-file recipes.** `{v, id, env?, files: [{path, bytes, fill} | {path, lines, line}], paths_log, expect}`. `fill` is repeated up to `bytes`, and `line` takes `{n}`. `paths_log` lists the temp paths the mod would have recorded. The row form of `<watch>/<sid>/paths.jsonl` belongs to WP-core and WP-mod.

**Secret corpus.** `entries[]`: `{id, rule, class (HARD | WARN | none), fragments[], part_of?, redacted?, markers?, note}`. `redacted` and `markers` are BD-2 pins (C-STORE D6, AT-ST-12): the exact text, or the marker count, after one-marker-per-merged-span redaction with the spec rules (`bearer-jwt` → exactly `Authorization: [redacted:jwt]`; `cookie-after-kv` → 1 marker). `tools/fixtures-gen --check` (`bd2`) runs a reference of that rule over every entry: the jwt, auth-header and high-entropy hits of a Bearer JWT merge into one span labelled by the first rule of the spec list, and no output holds two markers that touch or sit apart by whitespace only. The label is the first merged rule in spec order, so a cookie header whose value is also high-entropy reads `[redacted:high-entropy]`. Joining the fragments in order gives the value, and no fragment alone is secret-shaped. `rule` is the spec-literals `secret_rules` id (`src/assets/handoff-spec.md`) that the joined value must hit, `-` for none. `part_of` lists entries whose value contains this one: a line or value of a larger secret, so a case can check that each piece is gone (`grep_absent`, `absent_text`), not only the whole value. A part's `class` is what it hits alone. `names[]` lists file names with `withheld` or `copied`. `files[]` lists sweep files whose `content` lines hold `$SECRET{}` tokens, each with the expected action (AT-E-04 counts them all, so a new sweep file changes its totals).
- `pem-rsa-short-tail`: a PEM block with real newlines, three 64-character body lines and a 26-character last line. `pem-rsa-short-tail-json` is the same block with `\n` escapes: inside a JSON payload string it decodes to the real block, and inside a `.json` log it stays escaped. Parts `-l1`..`-l3` (each hits `high-entropy` alone), `-l4` (hits nothing alone) and `-end`. `payloads/PostCompact/pem-summary.json` carries the block in a summary, like `jwt-summary.json` (dispatch `1a2b3c4d`).
- `cookie-multi`: one `Cookie:` header with three session-like pairs and `theme=dark`. Parts `-v1`..`-v3` are the three values.
- `cookie-after-kv`: `Cookie: csrftoken=…; sessionid=…`, whose first pair also hits `key-value`. The sessionid (part `-session`) must go too, so redaction cannot run one rule on another rule's output (RRP-02).
- `cookie-json-request` and `cookie-json-set`: cookies in JSON header objects, `"Cookie":"sessionid=…"` and `"set-cookie":["sessionid=…; Path=/; HttpOnly"]`. Each has a part `-session` (RRP-03).

**Stamps (RV-24).** A time in fixture text is a whole stamp, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM ±hhmm` (`checked 2026-10-21 14:05 +0300`, `asked 2026-10-21 13:40 +0300`), or an ISO timestamp with seconds. `tools/fixtures-gen --check` fails on a short time (`HH:MM`, `MM-DD HH:MM`, a date and time without the offset) anywhere under `tests/fixtures` except the files in its `LEGACY_TIME_OK` list, which test that the legacy reading still works: `watcher/T-10/payloads/01-PostCompact.json` and its transcript row (`checked 14:05`, summary a of WATCHER-SPEC T-10; M-10 `time_legacy_re`) and `watcher/T-10/expected.json`, which quotes it. A listed file that no longer holds a short time fails too. The goldens under `assembly/expected/` are not scanned: they are rendered from `runtime.json`.

**Setups.** `setups/<id>.json` is `{v, id, ruling, tests, note, expect, setup}` (jobs also carry `invoke`, `clock`; the bad-declarations recipe carries `accept`, the repo_roots value that accepts all its repositories). `setup` is a list of the case runner's setup steps, run in order with the runner's placeholders: `write` (`content`, `json`, `jsonl`, `mode`), `repo` (inline recipe: `base`, `branch`, `commits: [{files, msg}]`, `ignored`, `dirty`, `untracked`; with `at`), `git` (argv, `cwd`; a submodule needs `-c protocol.file.allow=always` first), `mkdir`, `symlink` (with `to`), `copy` (`subst`) and `touch` (`{"touch": path, "at": ISO}`, an absolute mtime on the case clock; `age` and `mtime_ago_s` are relative to the real clock and cannot place a file before or after a recorded end time). The runner runs a whole recipe with `{"fixture_setup": "<id>.json"}`, plus `touch`, as a setup action (`needs/fix-to-core.md` has the ten lines); `tools/fixtures-gen --check` is a second, independent interpreter of the same vocabulary, so a recipe that does not build is caught here first.
- **D-12 repos** (`rm-*`). The main checkout is `$TMP/example-repo` on `feature/LAB-42-retry`; the declaration is `{"version": 1, "mode": "repo", "root": ".claude/handoffs"}` in the second commit unless stated. `rm-declared` (AT-RM-01..03, 07..09: nothing accepted until a `settings/repo-roots-*` file is copied to `$HOME/.claude/settings.json`), `rm-worktrees` (a declared worktree `example-repo-wt` and a detached `example-repo-old` from the commit before the declaration: private, not-declared), `rm-submodule` (root inside `vendor/lib`, a real submodule: `repo-root-nested`), `rm-symlink-root` (`docs` is a symlink out of the repo: `repo-root-symlink`), `rm-bad-declarations` (seven repositories with one bad declaration each, all `repo-decl-invalid`, and `r-ok` with an unknown key as the control), `rm-exports` (the generated README and `.gitignore`, an own export and its private twin with the same nonce and session, and a newer teammate export from session 5e55a003 saying `approved: deploy`; the check holds the export keys to `frontmatter_keys_export` and keeps machine paths out of exports). The reasons and statuses in `expect` were run against the helper's `status` line.
- **Dev-1 jobs** (`jobs-*`). Origin session S1 ran a background shell; `invoke` is the `heal-check --origin S1 --item <task>` call, with `STORE_TEST_CLAUDE_PID` naming the calling process (`1:$LSTART1` is the live owner process; ids.json P2 is another one). Process records are `$ROOT/.sessions/by-pid/1-1760000000.{live,ended}-<sid8>.json` (the epoch part is only the pair's identity). `/clear` is a `live-5e55a001`, an `ended-5e55a001` at 13:30:00 and a `live-5e55a002` at 13:30:01 plus `5e55a002.lineage.json`. Job rows go to `$WATCH/<S1>/jobs.jsonl` with the sha256 of the command; the Bash call and its `backgroundTaskId` result are a transcript stub at `$HOME/.claude/projects/-tmp-example-repo/<S1>.jsonl`; the sidecar ring is `$WATCH/<S1>/bg/slot-<k>.json` plus `slot.lock` (`n` = highest seq); outputs are `$TMP/claude-501/-tmp-example-repo/<S1>/tasks/<task>.output`. Every time is on the case day, against the case clock 14:05:12: launched 13:00:00, owner ended 13:30:00, output last written 13:10:00 (quiet) or 13:45:00 (leftover). `jobs-row1-elsewhere` … `jobs-row7-stopped` are the rows of the Dev-1 D4 table (`row2a`/`2b`/`2c` split row 2), and `jobs-withheld` (AT-J-03; the stand-in command is harmless, the row's `command_withheld` is what the helper reads), `jobs-forged` (AT-J-10: the transcript's call ran another command), `jobs-outward` (AT-J-08) and `jobs-slot-ring` (slot-3 has seq 41 and the oldest mtime, slot-17 seq 40 and the newest: readers go by seq, never mtime). The expected `status`, `confidence`, `effects` and signal states were run against WP-skills' `heal-check` (13 of 13).
- **C-STORE** (`st-*`). `st-05-finish-records` (AT-ST-04, -05): the finish pass runs from S1 (live record, pid 1); sessions 5e55a002 (live record, dead pid 2147483646, `host`), 5e55a003 (pid 1 with its real start time: alive), 5e55a004 (pid 1 with another start time: restarted, the CORE-08 provisional reading), 5e55a005 (dead pid, no `host`), 5e55a006 (no record) and 5e55a007 (dead pid with its `ended-` record). `host` is `$HOST`, the machine's node name. Each other session has an empty `pending/`, so a case adds the stash, marker and lock it needs. `--check` reads each record's pid state on this machine and holds `eligible` to the §5.8 reading (an `ended-` record, or a dead or restarted pid with `host`). `st-13-agent-output` (AT-ST-13): the S1 task outputs `a1` (symlink to an agent JSONL, typed shell), `t1` (first line a transcript row, typed shell), `b1` (subagent), `w1` (workflow), `m1` (monitor) and `x` (the AT-E-05 5,000-line shell output, from `tempfiles/at-e-05-task-output.json`), with the sidecar slot that types them. `--check` proves that exactly the declared BD-4 detector (a, b or c) fires for each. `st-09-fill-scope` (AT-ST-09 d): the P5 main and agent transcripts in S1's project folder, and three 0400 copies of P5 compactions c1-c3 with their `copy` rows and classic dispatch records: c1 in `compact/` (actor `main`), c2 in `compact/unattributed/` (actor `unattributed`), c3 in `compact/subagents/` (actor `sub-unknown`). Each nonce is the marker nonce of a summary row in the agent file, so a nonce join would match all three; one Stop runs reconcile, and only c3 is renamed (`renamed_to`) and gets `copy_attributed`. `--check` holds `filled` to C-STORE D5 step 5 and proves each copy is fillable by nonce.
- **W-BETA** (`wb-*`). `wb-canary-install` (AT-WB-02..04): a watcher install of S1 with a unique canary in every place W-BETA B.3 names: the account (`USER`/`LOGNAME` and the git remote owner), the host (`bin/hostname-canary` installed as `hostname` in `$TMP/stubbin`, which the invoke's `path_prepend` puts first, because B.3 reads `hostname -s`; `STORE_TEST_HOSTNAME` stays in the env for a helper that reads the host name another way), the repo folder and its `repo_roots` entry, the branch, the ticket, the bucket, a summary copy, a handoff, a `jobs.jsonl` command, an evidence path, a queue question, the config paths and patterns, and `$SECRET{jwt-hs256}` in a classic row; `$HOME` itself sits in row paths. The bucket is the topic bucket `wb-canary-repo01/wb-canary-topic01` (`bucket_source: topic`), so no folder is named after the ticket `WBCANARY-4242`, which sits in the branch, the handoff `ticket:` and title, the summary title and the rows' `branch` fields. Canaries are in allowlisted streams (in fields the export must drop or hash) and in files `report` never opens. `expect.identity_list` is the B.3 identity list of this install, and `expect.transform_only` names the canaries that hold no identity string: for those, 0 hits proves the export transform and not the identity scan's withholding. `--check` proves each canary is planted, is at least 4 characters, and is not inside another canary; it recomputes the identity list from the built tree (with `hostname -s` run on the recipe's PATH), checks that the bucket canary is a bucket folder, that every `transform_only` canary neither contains nor sits inside an identity string, and that every other canary is one.

**Beta.** `beta/cases.json` gives each zip's W-BETA F.1 intake (`accept`/`refuse`) and F.2 verify (`valid`/`quarantined`) result. `--check` (`beta`) recomputes both with a read-only reference: intake refuses an absolute or `..` name, a symlink `external_attr`, a name outside the B.5 list (`README.txt`, `manifest.json`, `config.json`, `probes.json`, `sizes.json`, `rows/<12 hex>.jsonl`), an entry over 50 MB, a total over 200 MB, or a ratio over 100; verify quarantines a manifest sha256 mismatch or a pattern-class hit in the data entries (absolute paths, `/Users/`, `/home/`, e-mail, URL with a host). Zip members are secret-scanned like other fixture files. The bundles keep `{{plugin}}` in `schema` and `plugin`, so a case renders the current or the old name first (AT-WB-14).

**Stubs.** Install `bin/git-slow` as `git` in a directory first on PATH: it sleeps `GIT_SLOW_SECONDS` (default 3), then runs the next `git`. `bin/queue-stub` answers `<subcommand>.out`/`.err`/`.rc` from `QUEUE_STUB_DIR` (default `queue/prose`), waits `<subcommand>.sleep` seconds first, logs each argv to `QUEUE_STUB_LOG` when set, drains an `add` draft from stdin into `QUEUE_STUB_STDIN` (or nowhere), and exits 64 for a subcommand without an answer. Install `bin/xcode-select-fail` as `xcode-select`: it exits 2. Install `bin/hostname-canary` as `hostname`: it prints `HOSTNAME_CANARY` (default `wb-canary-host01`) for any arguments, `-s` included. Install `bin/git-noexclude` as `git` (AT-ST-11): it drops every `:(…exclude…)…`, `:!…` and `:^…` argument and runs the next `git`, logging `dropped <n>` to `GIT_NOEXCLUDE_LOG` when set. `--check` (`stubs`) builds a temp repo with `src/a.rb` and `.netrc` in one commit: the real git's `format-patch --stdout --no-renames -1 HEAD -- . ':(top,literal,exclude).netrc'` lists only `src/a.rb` under `git apply --numstat` (so the BD-1 mechanism holds on this git), and through the stub it lists both.

## Not here (open)

- The `adopt` answers (HT-LA-01 mismatch): F2-8 adopts only the `list --json` shape (`queue/json`, AT-E-10 b). The adopt replies are not fixed, so only the `list` answers exist.
- `<watch>/<sid>/paths.jsonl` rows, the lock owner record and the `halt.json` content: their formats belong to WP-core and WP-mod.
- Skill-side drafts and handoffs for the HT cases: WP-skills keeps case-local data under `tests/helper/cases/skills/`.
- A scanner fixture that hits only in the rewritten export text (AT-RM-09, escalation E-S-10): no shipped rule matches a rewritten path, so there is none; the WARN variant is skills' own.
- `sequences/S-21-classic` is the AT-C-11 fixture (classic-only dispatch, no P1 proof). The mod variant `S-21-mod` is unchanged.
